title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: o dever dos gatos
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: the duty of cats

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

The Secrets of Cats apresenta gatos sapientes que protegem seus humanos, chamados de Fardos, contra espíritos, monstros, animais perigosos e outros gatos. A sociedade felina é territorial, política e secreta, e o primeiro dever é impedir que humanos descubram o que os gatos fazem.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Mundo oculto: animais sapientes conversam entre si, espíritos habitam lugares comuns e mitos humanos guardam fragmentos de verdade.
  • Fardos: cada gato protege uma pessoa, família ou comunidade que não entende o perigo ao redor; cuidar desse vínculo cria tanto recursos quanto complicações.
  • Parlamento dos Gatos: cada região tem um conselho que arbitra disputas, organiza patrulhas e reage a questões atuais e iminentes, apesar da dificuldade de organizar animais territoriais.
  • Vida felina: território, patrulha, treinamento, abrigo, resgate de animais e política local dão objetivos entre uma ameaça sobrenatural e outra.
  • Magia felina: nomes verdadeiros ligam palavra e alvo; sacrifícios podem ampliar rituais, mas nunca devem usar um ser sapiente. Warding, Naming, Shaping e Seeking são as quatro escolas.

Como aproveitar

Construa a campanha pela perspectiva de um gato. O que parece banal para uma pessoa pode ser um mistério enorme, e o que parece uma missão heroica pode começar com proteger um Fardo dormindo.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The Secrets of Cats presents sapient cats who protect their humans, called Burdens, from spirits, monsters, dangerous animals, and other cats. Feline society is territorial, political, and secretive, and its first duty is keeping humans from learning what cats do.

Sections and tools

  • Hidden world: sapient animals speak to one another, spirits inhabit ordinary places, and human myths preserve fragments of truth.
  • Burdens: each cat protects a person, family, or community that does not understand the danger around it; the bond creates both resources and complications.
  • Parliament of Cats: each region has a council that arbitrates disputes, organizes patrols, and responds to current and impending issues despite cats’ resistance to organization.
  • Feline life: territory, patrols, training, shelter, animal rescue, and local politics provide objectives between supernatural threats.
  • Feline magic: true names link word and target; sacrifices can strengthen rituals, but never use a sapient being. Warding, Naming, Shaping, and Seeking are the four schools.

How to use it

Build the campaign from a cat’s perspective. What is ordinary to a person can be a huge mystery, and a heroic mission may begin by protecting a sleeping Burden.

title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: criação de personagens
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: character creation

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

A ficha felina usa cinco aspectos e uma pirâmide de perícias compacta. Conceito, problema, Fardos, Nome Verdadeiro e aspecto livre definem uma criatura competente, mas ainda distraída, curiosa e limitada pela forma como gatos enxergam humanos.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Aspectos: o conceito alto inclui o título da escola dominada; o problema cria drama; Fardos definem quem é protegido; o Nome Verdadeiro é uma identidade íntima e perigosa; o aspecto livre conecta a personagem a outra história.
  • Perícias: uma Great, duas Good, três Fair e quatro Average. Athletics, Burglary, Deceive, Empathy, Fight, Investigate, Lore, Notice, Physique, Provoke, Rapport, Stealth, Territory e Will formam a lista.
  • Territory: substitui Contacts e Resources, mede domínio territorial, informação, respeito e acesso a recursos. Perder um conflito pode deixar um aspecto de território roubado até a personagem recuperar a área.
  • Magia e Recarga: Recarga 3, três façanhas mágicas e três normais; estresse mental e físico começam com duas caixas cada, e consequências seguem Fate Core.
  • Ser gato: visão noturna, faro, audição, garras e equilíbrio são verdades narrativas; alfabetização limitada, distrações e estranheza diante do mundo humano são convites para forçar aspectos.

Como aproveitar

Escreva o Nome Verdadeiro como algo conquistado por ações. Ele deve revelar quem o gato se tornou e criar uma pergunta sobre o que aconteceria se um inimigo o descobrisse.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The feline sheet uses five aspects and a compact skill pyramid. High concept, trouble, Burdens, True Name, and a free aspect define a competent creature still distracted, curious, and limited by the way cats see humans.

Sections and tools

  • Aspects: high concept includes the title of the mastered school; trouble creates drama; Burdens define who is protected; True Name is intimate and dangerous; the free aspect connects the character to another story.
  • Skills: one Great, two Good, three Fair, and four Average. Athletics, Burglary, Deceive, Empathy, Fight, Investigate, Lore, Notice, Physique, Provoke, Rapport, Stealth, Territory, and Will form the list.
  • Territory: replaces Contacts and Resources, measuring territory, information, respect, and access to resources. Losing a conflict can leave a stolen-territory aspect until the character wins it back.
  • Magic and Refresh: Refresh 3, three magical stunts, and three normal stunts; physical and mental stress begin with two boxes each, with Fate Core consequences.
  • Being a cat: night vision, scent, hearing, claws, and balance are narrative truths; limited literacy, distractions, and human strangeness invite compels.

How to use it

Write the True Name as something earned through actions. It should reveal who the cat became and create a question about what happens if an enemy learns it.

title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: escolas de magia
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: schools of magic

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

As quatro perícias mágicas transformam o Nome Verdadeiro em proteção, controle, mudança corporal e conhecimento. Uma escola pode ser dominada, mas as demais continuam úteis em níveis menores; magia fraca sempre cobra um preço sério.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Warding: cria círculos, barreiras, proteção contra espíritos e defesas para Fardos. O título Warden permite façanhas exclusivas e os melhores efeitos defensivos.
  • Naming: altera, anima ou controla alvos cujo Nome Verdadeiro é conhecido. A escola trabalha com ataques mentais, ordens, maldições e negociação de identidade.
  • Shaping: muda o próprio corpo por uma cena, cria vantagens físicas, permite disfarces e, para um Shaper, formas como sombra ou mudanças radicais de tamanho.
  • Seeking: encontra pessoas, objetos e caminhos; lê resíduos emocionais com Psychometry, visita sonhos com Dreamwalking, prevê pistas e projeta a forma astral.
  • Escalas e custos: gatos, ratos, cães, humanos e outros seres usam uma escada de tamanho; sangue, tempo, links e consequências tornam cada grande ritual uma escolha.

Como aproveitar

Faça o Nome Verdadeiro importar na ficção antes de convertê-lo em bônus. O melhor ritual é aquele que exige uma descoberta, uma aproximação ou um sacrifício que a Mesa não esquecerá.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The four magic skills turn a True Name into protection, control, bodily change, and knowledge. One school can be mastered while the others remain useful at lower levels; weak magic always carries a serious cost.

Sections and tools

  • Warding: creates circles, barriers, spirit protection, and defenses for Burdens. The Warden title unlocks exclusive stunts and the strongest defensive effects.
  • Naming: changes, animates, or controls targets whose True Name is known. The school handles mental attacks, commands, curses, and identity bargains.
  • Shaping: changes the cat’s body for a scene, creates physical advantages, enables disguises, and lets a Shaper take forms such as shadow or radically altered size.
  • Seeking: finds people, objects, and routes; reads emotional residue with Psychometry, visits dreams with Dreamwalking, glimpses prophecy, and projects an astral form.
  • Scale and cost: cats, mice, dogs, humans, and other beings use a size ladder; blood, time, links, and consequences make every major ritual a choice.

How to use it

Make the True Name matter in the fiction before turning it into a bonus. The best ritual requires a discovery, an approach, or a sacrifice the table will remember.

title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: Silver Ford
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: Silver Ford

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

Silver Ford é uma cidade pequena, antiga e cheia de lugares onde o mundo humano toca o mundo oculto. O capítulo fornece questões, lugares e rostos para uma campanha além da aventura Black Silver.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Questões: a cidade pode ter problemas atuais e iminentes ligados a território, atividade paranormal, crianças curiosas, animais capturados ou inimigos formando alianças.
  • Lugares: casas, ruas, bosque, mina de prata, abrigo de animais e pontos de encontro oferecem zonas com aspectos e rotas para patrulhas.
  • Rostos: membros do Parlamento, Fardos, animais sapientes, espíritos e moradores humanos permitem que cada pista tenha uma relação em vez de ser apenas informação.

Como aproveitar

Apresente Silver Ford por sons, cheiros e rotas de gato. A cidade fica mais viva quando cada lugar tem uma fronteira territorial e cada rosto quer algo dos protagonistas.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

Silver Ford is a small, old town full of places where the human world touches the hidden one. This chapter provides issues, locations, and faces for a campaign beyond the Black Silver adventure.

Sections and tools

  • Issues: current and impending problems can involve territory, paranormal activity, curious children, captured animals, or enemies forming alliances.
  • Places: homes, streets, woods, the silver mine, animal shelter, and meeting points offer zones with aspects and patrol routes.
  • Faces: Parliament members, Burdens, sapient animals, spirits, and human residents make every clue a relationship rather than mere information.

How to use it

Present Silver Ford through feline sounds, scents, and routes. The town feels alive when every place has a territorial boundary and every face wants something from the protagonists.

title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: Black Silver
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: Black Silver

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

Black Silver é a aventura central: crianças entram em uma mina abandonada no Halloween, libertam um mal antigo e deixam os gatos entre proteger seus Fardos, entender a história local e conter uma ameaça que envolve ratos, fantasmas e magia.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Abertura: sinais no território e o comportamento estranho dos Fardos levam os gatos a investigar antes que os humanos percebam o perigo.
  • Ratos e lugar escuro: seguir ou interrogar os ratos abre caminhos diferentes; a mina funciona como cenário, ameaça e fonte de pistas.
  • Manhã seguinte: consequências aparecem nos Fardos e no Parlamento, exigindo que a Mesa conecte a investigação noturna à vida cotidiana.
  • Preço de Hieronymous e história local: um espírito ou antigo agente oferece informação mediante troca, enquanto a história de Silver Ford revela o que alimenta a assombração.
  • Fantasma Ardente e Rei dos Ratos: o clímax pode ser resolvido com conflito, Nome Verdadeiro, Warding, alianças ou uma escolha sobre qual parte do mal deve ser selada.

Como aproveitar

Não trate a aventura como uma sequência obrigatória de combates. Deixe cada escola de magia e cada Fardo oferecer uma forma diferente de descobrir o que aconteceu.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

Black Silver is the central adventure: children enter an abandoned mine on Halloween, release an old evil, and leave the cats balancing Burden protection, local history, and a threat involving rats, ghosts, and magic.

Sections and tools

  • Opening: territorial signs and strange Burden behavior lead the cats to investigate before humans notice the danger.
  • Rats and the dark place: following or questioning the rats opens different routes; the mine is setting, threat, and clue source.
  • The next morning: consequences appear among Burdens and the Parliament, connecting the night investigation to daily life.
  • Hieronymous’s price and local history: a spirit or former agent offers information in exchange for something, while Silver Ford’s history reveals what feeds the haunting.
  • Burning Ghost and Rat King: the climax can use conflict, True Name, Warding, alliances, or a choice about which part of the evil must be sealed.

How to use it

Do not treat the adventure as a mandatory sequence of fights. Let each magic school and each Burden offer a different way to discover what happened.

title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: complicações e ameaças
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: complications and threats

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

O capítulo final de material de campanha amplia Silver Ford com complicações e ameaças prontas. A proposta é variar o tipo de perigo: nem toda ameaça deve atacar um Fardo diretamente, e nem todo inimigo precisa ser derrotado pela força.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Complicações: território disputado, Fardos inconvenientes, rivalidade entre gatos, regras do Parlamento, animais capturados e sacrifícios difíceis mudam o custo de uma missão.
  • Ameaças: espíritos, animais sapientes, monstros e gatos corrompidos podem receber aspectos, perícias, estresse e consequências em escala proporcional ao papel que ocupam.
  • Segredo: a regra de não revelar o mundo oculto cria pressão social; humanos curiosos, crianças e testemunhas podem ser obstáculo, aliado ou futuro Fardo.

Como aproveitar

Combine uma ameaça externa com uma complicação interna. Assim os gatos precisam proteger alguém e decidir que tipo de comunidade querem ser.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The final campaign-material chapter expands Silver Ford with ready complications and threats. The goal is variety: not every threat should attack a Burden directly, and not every enemy must be defeated by force.

Sections and tools

  • Complications: disputed territory, inconvenient Burdens, feline rivalry, Parliament rules, captured animals, and difficult sacrifices change a mission’s cost.
  • Threats: spirits, sapient animals, monsters, and corrupted cats can receive aspects, skills, stress, and consequences scaled to their role.
  • Secrecy: the rule against revealing the hidden world creates pressure; curious humans, children, and witnesses can be obstacle, ally, or future Burden.

How to use it

Pair an external threat with an internal complication. The cats then have to protect someone and decide what kind of community they want to be.

title.pt: The Secrets of Cats: tabelas rápidas
title.en: The Secrets of Cats: quick tables

html.pt:
Mapa do livro

Esta é uma síntese editorial bilíngue das seções e ferramentas da edição fornecida. O texto protegido e o layout original não são reproduzidos; consulte a referência oficial para a obra completa.

As tabelas finais aceleram a criação de gatos e a preparação do Narrador. Elas geram Nomes Verdadeiros, Fardos, façanhas e complicações sem substituir a conversa sobre personalidade, território e relações.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Gerador de Nome Verdadeiro: resultados sugerem uma identidade conquistada por feitos, hábitos, escolhas e responsabilidades.
  • Gerador de Fardo: cria humanos ou grupos cuja proteção já começa com vínculo, necessidade e risco narrativo.
  • Gerador de façanha felina: mistura traços de gato, escolas mágicas e funções de investigação, defesa, mobilidade ou conflito.
  • Uso na Mesa: role uma tabela quando quiser uma semente imediata, mas ajuste o resultado para que o gato tenha voz e uma relação concreta com os demais.

Como aproveitar

Use as tabelas para iniciar uma conversa, não para encerrar a criação. Um resultado aleatório fica melhor quando alguém explica por que ele importa para o gato.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The final tables speed up cat creation and Game Master preparation. They generate True Names, Burdens, stunts, and complications without replacing discussion of personality, territory, and relationships.

Sections and tools

  • True Name generator: results suggest an identity earned through deeds, habits, choices, and responsibilities.
  • Burden generator: creates humans or groups whose protection already carries connection, need, and narrative risk.
  • Cat stunt generator: combines feline traits, magic schools, and investigation, defense, mobility, or conflict roles.
  • At the table: roll when an immediate seed helps, then adjust it so the cat has a voice and a concrete relationship with the group.

How to use it

Use the tables to begin a conversation, not end creation. A random result is stronger when someone explains why it matters to the cat.

Grimoire coloca a Mesa em Ganseldom, um mundo de city-states, guerra aristocrática e magia que só existe por meio de daemons. Bruxos servem nobres em segredo, usando grimórios para convocar criaturas poderosas enquanto a Igreja de Myros tenta erradicar a prática.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Sobrenatural: daemons são criaturas de outro mundo, amoralmente interessadas em seus próprios objetivos; rituais e pactos definem o que podem fazer no plano mortal.
  • Nobres e bruxos: patrões oferecem dinheiro, grimórios e proteção contra a Igreja; em troca, esperam espionagem, sabotagem e influência política.
  • Grimórios: cada tomo costuma chamar uma variedade específica ou um indivíduo único. A posse do livro é recurso, risco e evidência de uma rede clandestina.
  • Ganseldom e city-states: conselhos nobres, comércio, rivalidades, guerra, portos e a Igreja criam uma política em que informação vale tanto quanto magia.
  • Religião e Mysteries: Myros condena daemons, enquanto cultos menores preservam conhecimentos, relíquias e relações ambíguas com o sobrenatural.

Como aproveitar

Comece pela relação entre patrão, bruxo e daemon. A magia fica mais interessante quando cada favor resolve uma urgência e piora uma posição política.

Grimoire places the table in Ganseldom, a world of city-states, aristocratic war, and magic that exists only through daemons. Warlocks secretly serve nobles, using grimoires to summon powerful creatures while the Church of Myros tries to eradicate the practice.

Sections and tools

  • Supernatural: daemons are otherworldly creatures with their own amoral goals; rituals and bargains define what they can do in the mortal world.
  • Nobles and warlocks: patrons provide money, grimoires, and protection from the Church in exchange for espionage, sabotage, and political influence.
  • Grimoires: each tome usually summons one variety or unique individual. Possessing the book is resource, risk, and evidence of a clandestine network.
  • Ganseldom and city-states: noble councils, trade, rivalries, war, ports, and the Church create politics where information is as valuable as magic.
  • Religion and the Mysteries: Myros condemns daemons while smaller cults preserve knowledge, relics, and ambiguous supernatural relationships.

How to use it

Start with the relationship among patron, warlock, and daemon. Magic becomes more interesting when each favor solves an urgent problem while worsening a political position.

O bruxo é um agente competente por si só, mas suas escolhas ficam presas a tentação, conexão e dívida. A criação usa a pirâmide do Fate Core, renomeia Drive como Ride e transforma Lore em conhecimento de rituais e defesa contra daemons.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Aspectos: conceito alto, tentação, conexão, sua aventura e cruzando caminhos dão ao personagem objetivos e pontos de pressão; um aspecto de vínculo e quatro de barganha começam vazios.
  • Perícias: Ride cobre montarias e carruagens; Will defende o controle; Lore cria rituais, círculos de sal e wards; a pirâmide começa com teto Great e sobe para Superb após o primeiro marco maior.
  • Façanhas: três façanhas iniciais podem representar caça a daemons, espionagem, negociação, rituais ou influência; até duas adicionais podem custar Recarga.
  • Favors Owed: a trilha registra dívidas com criaturas que foram libertadas ou cujos pactos terminaram, criando obrigações que voltam em cenas futuras.

Como aproveitar

Escreva a tentação como algo que o personagem realmente quer, não como um defeito genérico. O daemon deve conseguir oferecer uma solução que pareça boa antes de cobrar o preço.

The warlock is capable alone, but their choices are tied to temptation, connection, and debt. Creation uses the Fate Core pyramid, renames Drive as Ride, and turns Lore into knowledge of rituals and daemon defenses.

Sections and tools

  • Aspects: high concept, temptation, connection, your adventure, and crossing paths give the character goals and pressure points; one bond aspect and four bargain aspects begin empty.
  • Skills: Ride covers mounts and carriages; Will defends control; Lore creates rituals, salt circles, and wards; the pyramid begins with a Great cap and rises to Superb after the first major milestone.
  • Stunts: three starting stunts can represent daemon hunting, espionage, bargaining, rituals, or influence; up to two more may cost Refresh.
  • Favors Owed: the track records debts to creatures whose bonds ended or whose pacts were broken, creating obligations that return in future scenes.

How to use it

Write temptation as something the character truly wants, not a generic flaw. The daemon should offer a solution that looks good before revealing its price.

Convocar um daemon exige materiais, tempo, grimório e uma intenção expressa por um aspecto de vínculo. Outro jogador cria e interpreta a criatura, transformando o servo em uma relação real dentro da Mesa, não em um simples equipamento.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Vínculo: o bruxo define uma finalidade como proteger, espionar ou destruir; o jogador escolhido usa essa frase para criar o conceito alto e a motivação do daemon.
  • Ficha do daemon: dois aspectos, cinco perícias, duas façanhas, três caixas de estresse e uma consequência leve; Glamours cria ilusões e Leverage mede a pressão sobre o controlador.
  • Exemplos: Daecaedia, The Weaver e Sanguinus mostram como força, conhecimento, espionagem, sedução, terror e rastreamento podem ocupar papéis diferentes.
  • Papel na ficção: daemons têm objetivos próprios, aceitam compels para obter pontos de destino e podem interpretar instruções de maneira literal ou interessada.

Como aproveitar

Dê ao jogador do daemon espaço para propor soluções e problemas. A convocação deve parecer uma negociação com uma pessoa perigosa, não uma ativação automática de poder.

Summoning a daemon requires materials, time, a grimoire, and an intention expressed by a bond aspect. Another player creates and portrays the creature, making the servant a relationship rather than simple equipment.

Sections and tools

  • Bond: the warlock defines a purpose such as protect, spy, or destroy; the chosen player uses the phrase to create the daemon’s high concept and motivation.
  • Daemon sheet: two aspects, five skills, two stunts, three stress boxes, and one mild consequence; Glamours creates illusions and Leverage measures pressure on the controller.
  • Examples: Daecaedia, the Weaver, and Sanguinus show how force, knowledge, espionage, seduction, terror, and tracking can fill different roles.
  • Fictional role: daemons have their own goals, accept compels for fate points, and may interpret instructions literally or self-servingly.

How to use it

Give the daemon’s player room to propose solutions and problems. Summoning should feel like bargaining with a dangerous person, not activating a power.

O pacto nunca é permanente. Bargain aspects oferecem poder imediato, mas aumentam Leverage; quando o bruxo sofre uma consequência ou o daemon é tirado de ação, a relação pode ruir e a dívida torna-se uma nova história.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Bargain aspects: cada compel aceito da tentação concede ponto de destino e uma invocação gratuita para uma façanha sobrenatural ou declaração de ficção.
  • Contestar controle: Leverage é duas vezes o número de aspectos de barganha; o daemon supera o vínculo e o bruxo defende com Will. Se vencer, leva barganhas e aumenta Favors Owed.
  • Daemon tirado de ação: a ligação é rompida, o bruxo sofre consequência moderada e não pode convocar outro até se recuperar; conceder evita parte do custo.
  • Ação em conflito: o daemon não rola iniciativa. O bruxo usa sua ação para comandá-lo, então somente um dos dois age a cada rodada, salvo façanhas especiais.
  • Façanhas avançadas: Dominant Will, Expert Bargainer, Major Daemon Summoning e Duplicate Pacts mudam controle, qualidade ou quantidade, sempre com pré-requisitos e riscos.

Como aproveitar

Mostre a dívida antes da ruptura. Quando um jogador aceita uma barganha, registre qual desejo foi explorado e que favor o daemon poderá exigir depois.

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The pact is never permanent. Bargain aspects provide immediate power while increasing Leverage; when the warlock takes a consequence or the daemon is taken out, the relationship can collapse and debt becomes a new story.

Sections and tools

  • Bargain aspects: each accepted compel on temptation grants a fate point and a free invoke for a supernatural stunt or fictional declaration.
  • Contesting control: Leverage equals twice the number of bargain aspects; the daemon overcomes the bond and the warlock defends with Will. If it wins, it takes bargains and increases Favors Owed.
  • Daemon taken out: the bond breaks, the warlock suffers a moderate consequence, and cannot summon another until recovery; conceding avoids part of the cost.
  • Conflict action: a daemon does not roll initiative. The warlock spends their action commanding it, so only one acts each exchange unless special stunts change that.
  • Advanced stunts: Dominant Will, Expert Bargainer, Major Daemon Summoning, and Duplicate Pacts alter control, quality, or quantity with prerequisites and risks.

How to use it

Show the debt before the break. When a player accepts a bargain, record which desire was exploited and what favor the daemon may demand later.

As facções transformam o cenário em uma teia de lealdades. Casas nobres, Igreja de Myros, cultos dos Mysteries, comerciantes e rivais oferecem patronagem, informação, proteção e ameaças que não podem ser resolvidas por um único ritual.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Patronos: uma casa nobre pode financiar o bruxo e, ao mesmo tempo, usar sua vida como garantia; favores políticos sempre vêm com testemunhas e consequências.
  • Igreja: a perseguição aos daemons é pública, mas decisões internas são atravessadas por corrupção, medo e disputas sobre quem tem autoridade.
  • Mysteries: cultos preservam grimórios e daemons únicos, negociando segredos com objetivos espirituais próprios.
  • Rivalidade: bruxos ligados a casas diferentes podem ser colegas, informantes, inimigos ou aliados temporários.

Como aproveitar

Dê a cada facção uma coisa que ela protege, uma coisa que deseja e uma coisa que teme. Isso cria negociação antes de qualquer combate.

Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The factions turn the setting into a web of loyalties. Noble houses, the Church of Myros, Mysteries cults, merchants, and rivals offer patronage, information, protection, and threats no single ritual can solve.

Sections and tools

  • Patrons: a noble house may fund a warlock while using their life as collateral; political favors always bring witnesses and consequences.
  • Church: persecution of daemons is public, but internal decisions are shaped by corruption, fear, and authority disputes.
  • Mysteries: cults preserve grimoires and unique daemons, trading secrets for their own spiritual purposes.
  • Rivalry: warlocks tied to different houses may be colleagues, informants, enemies, or temporary allies.

How to use it

Give every faction something it protects, wants, and fears. That creates negotiation before any combat.

A aventura The Rise of House Volio coloca os bruxos no centro de uma disputa de poder. Rumores, chantagem, rivalidade entre casas, santuário religioso e um ataque à propriedade Fiora permitem jogar política e magia como frentes simultâneas.

Seções e ferramentas

  • Volio Manor: a nova casa tenta conquistar um assento e precisa de agentes capazes de descobrir alianças, provas e fraquezas sem expor o próprio patrão.
  • True Dominion Sanctuary: a Igreja e os cultos oferecem rotas opostas para lidar com daemons, fé e legitimidade.
  • Raid on the Fiora Estate: a operação transforma espionagem em conflito e exige decidir o que roubar, revelar ou preservar.
  • Personagens e facções: o Narrador recebe motivos e relações para mudar o rumo conforme os jogadores negociam, fazem barganhas ou deixam um daemon agir por conta própria.
  • Continuação: o resultado pode elevar House Volio, iniciar uma guerra de sucessão, libertar uma criatura ou tornar os protagonistas devedores de um poder que não controlam.

Como aproveitar

Apresente a aventura como uma oportunidade real de ascensão. Se os personagens vencerem, a política deve mudar; se falharem, a dívida e a perseguição devem mudar também.
html.en:
Book map

This is a bilingual editorial summary of the supplied edition’s sections and tools. Protected text and the original layout are not reproduced; use the official reference for the complete work.

The Rise of House Volio puts warlocks at the center of a power struggle. Rumors, blackmail, rival houses, a religious sanctuary, and a raid on the Fiora estate let politics and magic operate on simultaneous fronts.

Sections and tools

  • Volio Manor: the new house seeks a seat and needs agents who can uncover alliances, evidence, and weaknesses without exposing their patron.
  • True Dominion Sanctuary: the Church and cults provide opposing routes through daemons, faith, and legitimacy.
  • Raid on the Fiora Estate: the operation turns espionage into conflict and asks what to steal, reveal, or preserve.
  • Characters and factions: the Game Master receives motives and relationships that can shift as players negotiate, bargain, or let a daemon act independently.
  • Aftermath: success may elevate House Volio, begin a succession war, free a creature, or leave the protagonists indebted to power they cannot control.

How to use it

Present the adventure as a real chance at advancement. If the characters win, politics should change; if they fail, debt and pursuit should change too.

html.pt:
Texto oficial integral em inglês

Este SRD ainda não possui uma tradução aberta em português incorporada ao projeto. O original completo aparece abaixo, preservado em inglês e sem tradução automática.

In this book, we talk about all sorts of disabilities, from visible to invisible, from mental illness to people who use wheelchairs. We talk about the mechanics of how adaptive devices work in game, and how they work on a practical level. Basically, we get into as many specifics as possible.

We can’t go over every disability on the planet; that would be futile. When you look at the text in The Nitty Gritty of Specific Disabilities (page XX), it’s important to know a couple of things. Every disability has been addressed by someone who knows the topic because they live it. Lillian has schizophrenia and synesthesia; Elsa is blind, deaf, and has PTSD (yup, it’s a fun diagnostic party). This is deliberate; personal experience gives you better insight into how to play a character than a medical text can. It also means our advice might be flawed.

Gaming With Disabilities (page XX) gives you more information about how to do the research and learn from other people without hurting anyone, and it’ll help you bring people who already have disabilities to your table.

Some of what’s said here may feel like you’re being told what not to do, which isn’t necessarily the most Fate-y thing ever. The goal here is to help you (the player and the GM) come to a better place where disability inclusion looks more like it should—a way to experience new stories without the burden of harmful tropes. Sometimes the only way to do that is to stop doing the things you’ve always done before.

Sidebar: On Saying “No”

Brian is one of the system and mechanics developers for this book! He pops in and out with ways to flesh out your mechanics from a Fate-y perspective.

As Elsa said, some of the text in this book likely feels like we’re telling you what not to do, and that might feel contrary to the ethos of Fate. You’re supposed to say “yes,” aren’t you?

Here’s the thing: Fate is a respectful game. We don’t tackle topics if we can’t tackle them in a respectful way, and when we do tackle topics—especially sensitive, difficult topics—we do it with the goal of not causing harm. Sometimes that works, and sometimes it doesn’t.

This book aims to help your table do this for a specific set of topics. We want everyone to have fun, but in a way that doesn’t hurt anyone or make anyone feel like they are less important.

So try this trick: if you write an aspect or a stunt or whatever and someone else at the table says, “Hey, that aspect kind of hurts me. Do you mind changing it?” don’t approach that as them saying “no” to you. Approach it as an opportunity for you to learn, to come up with a better, more respectful way to express what you’re trying to express, or to realize that sometimes a trope is just plain harmful and shouldn’t be used at the table.

Remember that everyone at the table is there to have fun, and if something you do is causing someone pain or discomfort, you’re getting in the way of their fun. It’s okay for the table to say “no” to that kind of behavior. Because Fate is a respectful game.

—Brian

A Short List of Things You May Not Have Considered

  • Disabled people don’t always want to be cured.
  • Not all disabilities have a cure.
  • The Disability Binary is a lie. Most disabilities exist on a sliding scale. Not all blind people are totally blind, not all D/deaf people are totally D/deaf, a person in a wheelchair may be able to stand and walk short distances.
  • An adaptive device is a tool, sometimes an extension of or replacement for a body part. It is not a toy or a prop or a thing to be mocked.
  • Disability can be part of your identity, but it isn’t all of you either. Disabled people are Jewish, PoC, gay, straight, trans… Disabled people are just that. Complex people.
  • Pain is relative. Some kinds of pain don’t even rate for someone who has it all the time.
  • Disability is not one size fits all; it looks different on everyone, and everyone who has a disability handles their own differently. Even people with the same disability don’t all handle it in the exact same way.
  • Not all disabilities are visible. You might play a character with an invisible disability—their experience is still a disabled one.

Language and Identity

There are a few different ways that people with disabilities talk about ourselves. Some prefer person first language. What does that mean? It’s very simple: It means the word “person” goes before the disability, such as “a man with depression.” Some people feel that it helps them maintain their identity as a “person first, disability second.” Other people, including myself (Elsa), prefer to be called a blind woman or a disabled woman. It’s a matter of preference and practice. In my case, because I have never known a body other than a disabled one to be mine, I choose the language of disabled first. However, gaining a disability later in life does not mean that you would prefer person first language. When you’re creating a character with a disability, consider what language they might prefer or, for that matter, the language preferred for the world you’re playing in.

A Note on Aspects

A cornerstone of Fate is that you can choose the aspects that interest you as a player, and choose language that suits your thinking. Since good aspects can be compelled as well as invoked, phrase aspects in a useful, flexible way. A character might be Strong, but they might also be Built Like a Tank or Tiny but Mighty. The actual wording of the aspect is just the anchor point to hang your understanding of the character on. Consider jotting down a description of how the aspect is supposed to work, both when invoked and when compelled. After all, even aspects like Amazon Princess or World’s Greatest Detective can use a little description to nail down what they cover.

We hope this book helps you apply the same richness of thought to tweaking straightforward aspects like Blind Swordsman (like Zatoichi) or Depressed Green Monster (like Shrek) or Anxious Blue Thought (like Sadness from Inside Out). While this book provides more colorful aspects that might be used in lieu of those, more importantly, it provides tools to allow you to have a richer understanding of the idea you’re expressing. We’re not looking to police “good” and “bad” aspects, only to suggest that the more you understand, the better the experience will be for you and for everyone you play with.

GMs, never compel an aspect in such a way that it takes a player character out of the flow of the story. For example, do not compel an Agoraphobic to force a player to hide in a corner while the action is unfolding in a vast train station. Instead, provide ideas of choices that will lead to more possibilities for the character. For example, you can hold up a fate point and suggest: “Do you think your agoraphobia would drive you to seek a safe spot somewhere? The station master ran out of the office when the second alarm rang, and the ‘Employees only’ door is slightly ajar…”

Heroism and Overcoming

We encourage you to use the Fate Accessibility Toolkit to explore playing characters with disabilities in heroic situations. Rewrite the overcoming narrative—the narrative that as a disabled person you’re heroic because you manage to get out your front door. This is one of the narratives we’re trying to encourage players to leave behind, telling new stories. Always push to have your characters with disabilities be part of the story as people first—not because they’re disabled, but because they’re heroes.

The actual wording of the aspect is just the anchor point to hang your understanding of the character on. Consider jotting down a description of how the aspect is supposed to work, both when invoked and when compelled. After all, even aspects like Amazon Princess or World’s Greatest Detective can use a little description to nail down what they cover.

We hope this book helps you apply the same richness of thought to tweaking straightforward aspects like Blind Swordsman (like Zatoichi) or Depressed Green Monster (like Shrek) or Anxious Blue Thought (like Sadness from Inside Out). While this book provides more colorful aspects that might be used in lieu of those, more importantly, it provides tools to allow you to have a richer understanding of the idea you’re expressing. We’re not looking to police “good” and “bad” aspects, only to suggest that the more you understand, the better the experience will be for you and for everyone you play with.

GMs, never compel an aspect in such a way that it takes a player character out of the flow of the story. For example, do not compel an Agoraphobic to force a player to hide in a corner while the action is unfolding in a vast train station. Instead, provide ideas of choices that will lead to more possibilities for the character. For example, you can hold up a fate point and suggest: “Do you think your agoraphobia would drive you to seek a safe spot somewhere? The station master ran out of the office when the second alarm rang, and the ‘Employees only’ door is slightly ajar…”

Heroism and Overcoming

We encourage you to use the Fate Accessibility Toolkit to explore playing characters with disabilities in heroic situations. Rewrite the overcoming narrative—the narrative that as a disabled person you’re heroic because you manage to get out your front door. This is one of the narratives we’re trying to encourage players to leave behind, telling new stories. Always push to have your characters with disabilities be part of the story as people first—not because they’re disabled, but because they’re heroes.

Whether you’re playing a disabled character, creating a character with disabilities, GMing for disabled characters, or making your gaming space more accessible and welcoming for disabled players, this section covers a lot of things you should think about.

Playing Characters With Disabilities

The way disabilities are expressed in Fate Core comes from the choices you make in character and the way you use your skills to navigate the world around you. You won’t necessarily narrate using your white cane on the pavement unless it matters in the story, but you might narrate the experience of trying to find a clue with your hands and not your eyes. Your character in a wheelchair has the Athletics skill, but it’s used for other ways of getting around than running and jumping. When playing a character with disabilities within Fate, avoid embodying that character by using a prop; rather, shift the way you think about interacting with the world at large.

Physical Disabilities

Most people are familiar with the disabilities you assume you can see—those that require mobility devices or exterior help. They’re often the disabilities that people stare at, because they see something as different from them. Some of the disabilities covered in this book include blindness, deafness, paralysis, and amputation. The fact is, not all these disabilities are visible, though. A blind person might wear glasses, or they might only be blind in one eye and not both. A D/deaf person might wear invisible hearing aids, or have a cochlear implant. All these things change the visible nature of disability—and that’s before we get future tech involved!

Physical disabilities likely affect play the most in terms of physical actions—everything from being able to notice objects or find clues, to running from a pack of slavering beasts.

Sidebar: Capital D or lowercase d?

The term D/deaf is used to describe people across the spectrum of deafness and of participation in Deaf Culture. A person who is a “capital D Deaf” person likely uses sign language either as their primary language or to the exclusion of orally spoken language. A person with the “little d” designation likely uses oral language skills, lipreading, and hearing aids. D/deaf is often used as a shortcut to describe both groups who are similar but not exactly the same when it comes to communication.

Hard of hearing (HoH) refers to those who have trouble hearing some sounds; this can range from mild to severe and is often helped by amplification devices such as hearing aids. There’s a medical definition with a firm delineation, but culturally and personally the lines are more blurry. How do you know if someone is hard of hearing or deaf or Deaf? It depends on how they personally identify themselves.

Invisible Disabilities

An invisible disability may not be apparent at first blush—a condition which, for better or worse, isn’t seen as a part of you at a glance. Many of these disabilities are still physical in nature by the way they affect the body, but aren’t obvious at first sight.

It should be made clear that these disabilities are not things that someone could make up, or convince oneself of within the context of mental illness. Both mental illness and invisible disabilities are valid, and real, and things which should be taken seriously, not questioned for their validity. Unfortunately, this is a common reaction to such disabilities, especially ones around pain or around neurotypicality.

Sidebar: Multiple Disabilities

Each disability could be coupled with other disabilities. However, as someone who lives with three disabilities, I can tell you that it’s not an easy path—I don’t recommend it unless you have extensive understanding of all the disabilities in your character’s background.

However, there may be occasions where it seems fitting to have two disabilities overlap from the same cause. In this case, it may be wisest to start with the cause—an accident, an illness, etc.—and identify a few consequences. For example, a character who survived a serious car wreck may have a mobility disability and also have PTSD which manifests primarily around travel and transit.

Rather than develop a full set of aspects for each, you might take one aspect related to PTSD and focus the rest of the character’s disability-related mechanics on their mobility disability. Or consider that one disability may manifest as mechanics, while the rest are part of the narrative gameplay. Above all, remember that your character is a complex person and should not be defined primarily by their disabilities, even if they have several.

See Creating a Disabled Fate Character (page XX) for suggestions on how to balance the mechanics.

Mental Illness

In game design we have a really difficult relationship with mental illness. Games don’t have a great track record for representing mental illness well, or for treating people who have mental illnesses with respect.

A lot of that has to do with the language that we use in creating games. Sanity checks. Games set in horrifying psychiatric facilities. Flaws or character defects that make mental illness look scarier than it is. All these things have made the game table a very shaky place to talk about mental health—but I hope this book can dispel a little bit of that bad faith. When discussing mental illnesses, we do our best to talk about not just what mental health can look like in games, but how it might affect your character for real, not as a joke or as a punchline, but as a way to develop your character. To help address these concerns, each of the mental illness sections has been written by a person who lives with the mental health condition listed.

It’s common and easy to assume we’re familiar with mental health conditions based on the oversimplified and often joking way they’re portrayed and talked about in everyday conversation. How often have you seen an offhand comment about OCD that describes it as a quirk and doesn’t account for the reality of what it means to live with it? If you play a character with a mental illness, consider doing an internet search of medical sources to get an idea of what a clinical diagnosis looks like. Not every mental illness plays out exactly the way that the diagnosis is written, but it’s a helpful piece of information for you to have. As a note, clinical diagnostic criteria sometimes change, and the definitions often alter how people identify. Having your diagnosis be a moving target is also something to consider, because it may make your character less sure of what exactly they live with.

Sidebar: Don’t Diagnose the Table

Just because you’re given access to these tools to diagnose and play out your character’s mental illness does not mean you should use these tools to diagnose real live people. If you have concerns about a friend or family member’s mental health, consider giving them the tools to seek out help, rather than diagnosing them on your own.

Horror and Mental Health

When playing in a game that focuses on people’s realities being torn apart, such as Cthulhu Mythos-related games, players should pay attention to how trauma, or changes to the reality they ascribe to, affect them as a character. Rather than using “crazy” behavior to elicit humor, focus instead on how the things that shift your worldview change what you are and aren’t willing to do. A woman who believes so strongly in justice that she’s willing to do anything to uphold the law may have trouble looking herself in the mirror after having to kill a cultist who was attempting to sacrifice a virgin. A doctor who believes strongly in his Hippocratic oath might not be so comfortable with himself when he finds out that the body doesn’t actually work the way that he’s always learned it does. The worlds we create can have effects on the mental health of our characters without becoming a hilarious trope of what the media feeds us as comedy.

I see a lot of people playing “crazy” characters as the catharsis of humor in many horror games. They’re the ones who do silly things and who act like children; in that case mental illness is played as a trait that makes people unpredictable or funny. People will still do this—I can’t reach through the pages of this book and stop you—but I encourage you to consider how mental illness would actually affect a character running around in a world that no longer makes any sense.

Anchors: Tracking Mental Trauma

The mind is complex, and a mechanic like sanity points or a random mental illness chart simplifies it in a way that can be reductive and insulting to people who actually live with mental illness. If you think your game needs such a mechanic, consider this as an alternative.

When creating characters, each player chooses five aspects: a high concept, a trouble, and three anchors. Those anchors are things that stabilize them, that give them comfort, that prevent them from spiraling into despair. They can be relationships, daily rituals they engage in, beliefs they hold, personal items or places that are very important to them, or a variety of other grounding forces.

Whenever a player wants a better roll but has no way to improve that roll—they’re out of fate points, they have no applicable stunts, or they simply don’t have any relevant aspects—they can risk an anchor. Doing so provides the benefit of invoking an aspect, but it comes with a catch: if the player succeeds on their roll, they must change that anchor by the end of the scene. The new anchor can be related or entirely new, provided that it makes sense within the context of the game. If the character fails their roll, nothing happens to their anchors; they simply suffer the effects of failure. A character can risk each anchor only once on a single roll.

This system is less about penalizing players or “damaging their sanity” when they’re exposed to horrific things and more about modeling how people change when exposed to horrors. It’s not explicitly for modeling mental illness, but it can be used to do so in a way that’s more organic and respectful than sanity points or a random mental illness chart.

If you use this system, know that it relies heavily on depriving the players of fate points. Consider lowering players’ starting refresh and using compels sparingly.

Creating a Disabled Fate Character

There are a number of ways to make a character with a disability and have the disability represented in game mechanics. The first step in all of those ways is to have one of your character aspects (possibly your high concept but it doesn’t have to be) establish the disability, such as Paraplegic Sleuth or Autistics Think Outside the Box. This alone shows that your character’s disability is a part of them that you’d like to explore. If that’s as far as you want to go, it’s absolutely enough.

Components of a Disability

On the other hand, establishing a disability through an aspect opens up a wealth of options. These include additional aspects, stunts, conditions, and extras.

Aspects

You can make as many of your aspects as you wish incorporate your disability. Discussions of the various disabilities in Fate Accessibility Toolkit give plenty of example aspects specifically related to those disabilities, but some examples include:

Blind Champion of Queen Iranthi: Invoke to gain a bonus in combat, take advantage of the fact that you know the Queen personally, or declare that the flickering firelight doesn’t bother you (because you can barely see it anyway). Compel when an opponent uses your limited vision against you or when you’d rather be taking care of a different problem but duty to the Queen calls you away.

The Best Hearing Aids Fifty Bucks Can Buy: Invoke when you need to replace them inexpensively or when you need a bonus to hear that guy sneaking up on you. Compel when the cheap pieces of junk crackle with static or whistle with feedback.

Former Wheelchair Basketball Olympian: Invoke to gain a bonus in a chase or when you need to throw an object, or when your determination never, ever to quit gets you through a tough spot. Compel when “never quit” means you throw good effort after bad, or when your rival from the Australian team shows up with some payback on her mind.

Quality Earplugs: Invoke when you need to recover from an autistic meltdown or don’t want the incredibly loud sounds of that factory to stir up your migraine. Compel when your earplugs mean you don’t hear the warning your partner yells to you, or you miss that your phone is ringing.

Stunts

You can compose stunts related to your disability using your character’s usual stunt slots and refresh. Stunts can represent qualities of your disability, as well as adaptive devices (page XX) you use. See Fate Core's stunt chapter (Fate Core System, page 88) for extensive details about composing stunts, but some examples include:

Shotgun Prosthetic (Deceive): Your rigid prosthetic leg contains a shotgun barrel, triggered by a lever at your hip. When you’re seated, you may make an attack (with Weapon:3) using Deceive against a target in your zone that isn’t aware of this extra feature.

Pain Tolerance (Physique): Your many years of dealing with chronic pain have made you resilient to physical punishment. Once per session, at the cost of a fate point, you can reduce the severity of a moderate consequence that’s physical in nature to a mild consequence (if your mild consequence slot is free), or erase a mild consequence altogether.

Lip Reader (Notice): You are highly adept at reading lips. You gain +2 to overcome actions made with Notice to “eavesdrop” on someone from a distance, provided you can see their mouth.

Extras and Conditions

Extras (Fate Core System, Chapter 11) can be used to represent some adaptive devices, such as wheelchairs or cybernetic implants. Most extras have a cost that you need to meet in order to take it, such as skill ranks in a certain skill or spending a stunt slot.

A condition is… well… a temporary condition that your character might find themself in. Conditions have special rules that come into effect when they’re active, and have a way to recover from them to deactivate those rules. We talk a lot about conditions on page XX.

What Can I Add To My Character?

So, how many conditions, extras, and such can you take when you make your character? Your aspects, skills, and stunts work as usual. The parts of your disability represented by aspects, skills, and stunts fit into those frameworks no differently than non-disability related elements. Extras list a permission (typically an aspect) and a cost (typically a stunt slot or point of refresh, sometimes more). Many give you some free aspects and stunts, which don’t count against your usual slots. You can take as many extras as you can afford within that cost.

Conditions are a bit different. Some extras suggest (or even require) particular conditions, so take those, but we suggest that you take any that make sense to your conception of your character.

Remember that with the Fate Accessibility Toolkit, your aim should not be precise mechanical “balance,” where every disadvantage is evened-out by a concrete advantage somewhere else. Let your focus be on modeling in rules the parts of your character that you’d like to reflect in rules.

This goes for any mechanical part of the game, not just conditions. Game designers and writers who live with these disabilities have stressed throughout this book many times that every person’s disability is unique—so it would be ridiculous to have hard-and-fast rules about how, say, blindness works that apply the same way every time. Be flexible. Make the character on paper the way they are in your imagination.

Example: Creating Ma Bell

Laurel is playing in a 90s-era Hackers game. Her high concept is Aspie Phone Phreaker who goes by “Ma Bell.” As a trouble aspect, Laurel decides her character has an I Can Do It! attitude which often gets her in over her head. Sometimes this could be related to an autistic fixation, but it’s more often a consequence of her curiosity and love of experimentation. Ma Bell pulls off her hijinks because she Hears in Patterns and uses devices to exactly mimic the sounds she needs. This is a cooler use of a real life way in which Laurel experiences her autism. Laurel reminds the GM that she isn’t playing a stereotypical savant or someone with superpowers; Ma Bell’s talent is in reproducing the patterns she hears.

Since Ma Bell uses homemade gadgets to phreak, Laurel creates the stunt Sonic Scrounger. With this stunt, she can identify potential components even when she’s separated from her electronic devices without spending a fate point. Making a new gadget still requires a Craft check. Laurel draws on her own experience of making people uncomfortable by observing things which fall outside social norms to develop the stunt I Can’t Help But Notice; it uses her character’s Notice in place of Provoke to create an advantage by unsettling or upsetting the target.

Laurel adds condition Meltdown to her sheet and tells the GM it’s generally triggered for her character by auditory stimuli. She considers whether she wants to take any assistive devices as aspects or extras. In everyday life, her partner acts as a service human. But she decides that her character is more of a loner and that her gadgets are all focused around her trade. She may invoke some of her real-life autistic traits in engaging with her gadgets, but she doesn’t feel it needs to be mechanical.

Ma Bell

Example: Creating Professor Jenkins

Elsa is creating Professor Jenkins, a blind super sleuth in a mystery campaign set in the 1920s. She takes the high concept aspect Blind Mystery-Solving Literature Professor which establishes that she’s blind and is extremely well-read and highly educated. Another of her aspects is Glasses Like Soda Bottles; Elsa tells the GM that Jenkins has some vision in one eye but it’s limited to close-up work and then only with her strong glasses.

Next, she composes this stunt to represent one of her items of adaptive technology, using one of her character’s three free stunts:

  • Magnifiers (Investigation): Professor Jenkins’s glasses have a jeweler’s magnification lens that she can position in front of her usual lenses. With this lens, she gains +2 to overcome and create advantage Investigation actions when examining objects close-up and looking for tiny details.

Finally, she likes the look of the extra called White Cane, and decides to add it to her character. The White Cane extra costs one of her stunt slots (so that’s the second of the three free stunts), but it gives her two free stunts and an additional aspect that are related to her cane. It also requires the Without My Device condition.
